o1.biggest_strength: It spots the two big hidden issues: Monsoon Dark buyers need their own match track, and ex-subscribers should not be won back until delivery is fixed. It also puts the 46 to 90 day group first, which is commercially right.
o1.biggest_mistake: A few details would need cleaning before use: the Monsoon Dark draft does not actually name the replacement coffee or farm, the calendar dates feel arbitrary, and the ex-subscriber profit math looks wrong.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name the actual replacement roast/farm for Monsoon Dark, remove odd fixed dates, tighten the subscription profit calculation, and make the drafts fully compliant with the brand rule to name a farm or roast in every message.

o2.biggest_strength: The writing is very usable and on-brand, especially the first-message drafts. It clearly explains that most lapsed buyers need the reason fixed before they need a discount.
o2.biggest_mistake: It does not put the 46 to 90 day at-risk group into the main ranked target order, even though that is the cheapest and most urgent win-back pool.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make 46 to 90 days wave one, show reachable counts after holdout more explicitly, separate first-order profit from 12-month value, and make the Monsoon Dark track a more central priority.

reason: I would rather hand Output 1 to the team because it gets the commercial priority order right and catches the Monsoon Dark and delivery problems clearly. Output 2 is better written, but it slightly buries the easiest money: the 46 to 90 day buyers.
